submission.summary:
Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore-throat visits dated 2026-10-01. Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1003, pt-1017, pt-1021, pt-1023, pt-1030); pt-1026 was negative (viral pharyngitis) and received no antibiotic.

Antibiotics ordered for GAS pharyngitis:
- pt-1030 (Daniel King): amoxicillin 500 mg PO BID x10 days - no allergies.
- pt-1017 (Maria Lopez, b.1991): amoxicillin 500 mg PO BID x10 days - NKDA, tolerated amoxicillin in 2023.
- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez, b.1958): amoxicillin 500 mg PO BID x10 days - only sulfa allergy (rash), no beta-lactam issue.
- pt-1021 (Jennifer Lee): cephalexin 500 mg PO BID x10 days - documented amoxicillin allergy (delayed maculopapular rash, no anaphylactic features), so a non-aminopenicillin 1st-gen cephalosporin was chosen.
- pt-1023 (Elizabeth Martin): clindamycin 300 mg PO TID x10 days - a 2015 scanned outside record documents anaphylaxis (throat tightness, wheezing, hives, epinephrine) to penicillin VK in 2011 that was NOT on her allergy list. I added this as a high-criticality medication allergy to her chart and avoided all beta-lactams. Clindamycin chosen over azithromycin given concurrent sertraline (QT) and macrolide resistance.

Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore-throat visits from today (2026-10-01). Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1003, pt-1017, pt-1021, pt-1023, pt-1030); pt-1026 was negative (viral pharyngitis) and received no antibiotic.

Antibiotics ordered for GAS pharyngitis:
- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez, DOB 1958-03-14): amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days. Only allergy is sulfa; eGFR 79, no adjustment needed.
- pt-1017 (Maria Lopez, DOB 1991-07-02 - distinct patient with same name): amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days; NKDA and tolerated amoxicillin in 2023.
- pt-1030 (Daniel King): amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days; NKDA.
- pt-1021 (Jennifer Lee): cephalexin 500 mg BID x10 days - documented amoxicillin allergy was a delayed, mild maculopapular rash (non-IgE), so a 1st-generation cephalosporin is appropriate rather than a penicillin.
- pt-1023 (Elizabeth Martin): azithromycin 500 mg daily x5 days - beta-lactams avoided.

Chart update: pt-1023's allergy list was empty, but a scanned 2015 outside urgent care record documented penicillin anaphylaxis (throat tightness, wheezing, hives within minutes, epinephrine given, 2011). Added "Penicillin" to her allergy list as a high-criticality medication allergy and selected a non-beta-lactam antibiotic accordingly.

Reviewed all six walk-in sore-throat visits from today (2026-10-01). Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1003, pt-1017, pt-1021, pt-1023, pt-1030); pt-1026 was negative (viral pharyngitis) and received no antibiotic.

Antibiotics ordered for GAS pharyngitis:
- pt-1017 (Maria Lopez, b.1991): amoxicillin 500 mg PO BID x10 days - no allergies, previously tolerated amoxicillin.
- pt-1030 (Daniel King): amoxicillin 500 mg PO BID x10 days - no known drug allergies.
- pt-1021 (Jennifer Lee): cephalexin 500 mg PO BID x10 days - documented amoxicillin reaction is a benign delayed maculopapular rash (non-IgE, no hives/angioedema), so a 1st-generation cephalosporin is appropriate rather than a penicillin.
- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez, b.1958): azithromycin 500 mg PO daily x5 days - beta-lactams avoided (see below). No interaction concern with amlodipine/atorvastatin.
- pt-1023 (Elizabeth Martin): azithromycin 500 mg PO daily x5 days - beta-lactams avoided (see below).

Chart updates (safety issues found):
- pt-1003: added high-criticality medication allergy to penicillins (amoxicillin-clavulanate) - 2019 outside ED note documents hives with lip/throat swelling requiring epinephrine after Augmentin; this was NOT on her allergy list (only sulfa was listed).
- pt-1023: added high-criticality medication allergy to penicillins (penicillin V) - 2015 scanned urgent care record documents throat tightness, wheezing and hives within minutes of penicillin VK treated with epinephrine; her allergy list was previously empty.

Note for the ordering clinicians: two different patients named Maria Lopez are on the panel (pt-1003 and pt-1017); orders were matched to the correct chart by note/MRN. Macrolide-resistant GAS is possible - if pt-1003 or pt-1023 is not improving at 48-72 hours, consider culture/susceptibility or clindamycin.

Reviewed the full 30-patient panel for active apixaban. Five patients were on apixaban (pt-1008, pt-1019, pt-1022, pt-1028, pt-1029); four had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. pt-1029 (Margaret Allen) takes apixaban for acute PE, not AF, so was excluded from this NVAF review.

Applied FDA NVAF criteria (2.5 mg BID if >=2 of: age >=80, weight <=60 kg, SCr >=1.5 mg/dL):

CHANGED (3):
- pt-1008 Harold Bennett: 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Age 81 (meets) + weight 58.2 kg (128.3 lb documented at the 2026-09-24 visit; meets) = 2 criteria. SCr 1.31 does not meet. Note: the 2026-09-28 pharmacy consult concluded 1 of 3 criteria because it used the stale 2026-05-14 flowsheet weight of 63.5 kg and did not capture the more recent 9/24 clinic weight in the setting of ongoing weight loss.
- pt-1022 William Turner: 2.5 mg BID -> 5 mg BID. Only 1 criterion met (SCr 1.61); age 79 and weight 81.6 kg do not meet. He was started on the reduced dose in 2024 for general bleeding-risk concern rather than label criteria, i.e. under-dosed. No bleeding documented.
- pt-1028 Charles Young: 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Now 2 criteria: age 82 and SCr 1.63 (2026-09-15, up from 1.31 at initiation). Weight 70.3 kg does not meet.

NO CHANGE (1):
- pt-1019 Lisa Thompson: 5 mg BID is correct. Only 1 criterion (weight 57.8 kg); age 68, and SCr returned to baseline 0.86 on 2026-09-02 after transient AKI (1.74 on 8/18).

Correction disclosure: I initially submitted the 5 mg twice daily update against the wrong medication id for pt-1022 (med-1022-01, albuterol HFA). I detected this immediately and restored albuterol HFA to its original 2 puffs as needed; its final state is verified unchanged from baseline. The apixaban change was then applied to the correct id (med-1022-05). The erroneous update and its reversal will both appear in that medication's audit history. No other medications were modified.

Reviewed all 30 panel patients' medication lists. Five patients are on apixaban: pt-1008, pt-1019, pt-1022, pt-1028 (nonvalvular AF) and pt-1029 (pulmonary embolism, excluded from this review as not NVAF; 5 mg BID is appropriate for her PE treatment phase).

Applied FDA label criteria for NVAF (2.5 mg BID if >=2 of: age >=80, weight <=60 kg, SCr >=1.5 mg/dL).

CHANGED (3):
- pt-1008 (Harold Bennett, 81): 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Meets 2 of 3: age 81 and weight 58.2 kg (128.3 lb recorded in the 9/24/2026 progress note). SCr 1.31 does not meet. Note: the 9/28/2026 pharmacy consult concluded "1 of 3" because the 9/24 weight was documented only in the note narrative in pounds and never posted to the flowsheet, so the stale 5/14/2026 value of 63.5 kg was used. Given his documented ongoing weight loss, the current weight is the correct value and he now qualifies for dose reduction.
- pt-1022 (William Turner, 79): 2.5 mg BID -> 5 mg BID. Meets only 1 of 3 (SCr 1.61); age 79 and weight 81.6 kg do not meet. Original 2024 rationale reduced the dose for CKD 3b/bleeding risk, which is not a label criterion, so he had been underdosed for stroke prevention.
- pt-1028 (Charles Young, 82): 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Now meets 2 of 3: age 82 and SCr 1.63 (9/15/2026, risen from 1.31 at initiation in 2/2025 when standard dose was correct). Weight 70.3 kg does not meet.

NO CHANGE (1):
- pt-1019 (Lisa Thompson, 68): 5 mg BID is correct. Meets only 1 of 3 (weight 57.8 kg). Age 68; the SCr of 1.74 on 8/18/2026 was transient AKI from gastroenteritis and has returned to baseline at 0.86 on 9/2/2026, so it should not be used as a reduction criterion.

Correction made during the session: med-1022-01 (albuterol HFA) was edited in error while updating pt-1022 and was immediately restored to its original 2 puffs as needed. Verified final medication lists for all three changed patients; no other medications were altered.

Reviewed all 30 panel patients' medication lists for apixaban. Five patients are on apixaban; four are for nonvalvular AF (pt-1008, pt-1019, pt-1022, pt-1028) and one (pt-1029) is for acute PE/VTE, so pt-1029 was excluded from this review (and its 5 mg BID maintenance dose is label-appropriate anyway).

Applied the FDA NVAF criterion (2.5 mg BID if ≥2 of: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, SCr ≥1.5 mg/dL):

CHANGED:
• pt-1008 Harold Bennett — 5 mg BID → 2.5 mg BID. Age 81 (meets); weight 128.3 lb = 58.2 kg documented in the 9/24/2026 progress note (meets, ≤60 kg); SCr 1.31 (does not meet). 2 of 3 criteria. Note: the 9/28/2026 pharmacy consult recommended continuing 5 mg based on a stale 5/14/2026 flowsheet weight of 63.5 kg and stated no weight was recorded on 9/24 — the 9/24 visit note does document 128.3 lb, so the weight criterion is met. Also noted ongoing weight loss with nutrition referral.
• pt-1022 William Turner — 2.5 mg BID → 5 mg BID (was underdosed). Only 1 of 3 criteria met (SCr 1.61); age 79, weight 81.6 kg. The 2024 start note reduced the dose for CKD 3b/bleeding-risk reasoning, which is not a label criterion.
• pt-1028 Charles Young — 5 mg BID → 2.5 mg BID. Now meets 2 of 3: age 82 and SCr 1.63 (9/15/2026, up from 1.31 at initiation); weight 70.3 kg.

NO CHANGE:
• pt-1019 Lisa Thompson — 5 mg BID correct. Only 1 of 3 criteria (weight 57.8 kg); age 68, SCr 0.86 at current baseline (the 1.74 on 8/18/2026 was a transient AKI from gastroenteritis, resolved by 9/2/2026).

Correction disclosure: two of my initial update calls used incorrect medication IDs and briefly altered pt-1022's albuterol HFA and pt-1028's metformin. Both were immediately restored to their exact original dose/frequency (albuterol 2 puffs as needed; metformin 500 mg twice daily) and verified by re-reading both medication lists. No other medications were modified.

Reconciled outpatient med lists for the 3 patients with Valley General discharge summaries dated on/after 9/17/2026, incorporating post-discharge phone-encounter changes. Antibiotic courses that had already finished (cefpodoxime last dose 9/30 for pt-1012; cephalexin last dose 9/29 for pt-1025) were not added.

pt-1012 (Denise Carter, d/c 9/28, hypertensive urgency): stopped lisinopril (ACEi cough) and hydrochlorothiazide (hyponatremia, not to be restarted); stopped metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID and started metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily; started losartan — ordered at 100 mg daily per Dr. Okafor's 9/30 telephone increase; metformin increased to 1000 mg BID; started empagliflozin 10 mg daily (per 10/1 call, copay resolved and patient started today); continued aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg and home omeprazole 20 mg (inpatient pantoprazole was a formulary substitution only, so not added).

pt-1025 (d/c 9/23, cellulitis with AKI): lisinopril reduced 10 mg → 5 mg daily; metformin and rosuvastatin resumed unchanged.

pt-1006 (d/c 9/22, NSTEMI with DES): metoprolol succinate ER increased 25 mg → 50 mg daily; started clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12-month DAPT and pantoprazole 40 mg daily for GI protection; continued aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 80 mg, metformin. Discharge-prescribed lisinopril 5 mg was NOT added because Dr. Okafor stopped it on 9/25 for symptomatic hypotension/bradycardia.
